rules: Prefer a specific species, subspecies, morph, population, or named biological adaptation over a generic animal category.
Avoid generic topics such as 'frogs', 'owls', 'sharks', 'snakes', or 'birds' when a specific species with a stronger hook is available.
The title and script should name the species whenever footage and fact verification support it.

Prioritize unusual species, visually distinctive animals, rare adaptations, extreme behavior, unusual anatomy, survival mechanisms, mimicry, venom, camouflage, reproduction, feeding strategies, and sensory biology.
Do not select obscure species only for novelty; the topic still needs strong verified facts and enough high-quality video-first footage.
Rotate taxonomic groups and habitats across consecutive days: mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish, marine invertebrates, terrestrial invertebrates, and other unusual groups.
Avoid repeating the same species in nearby batches unless there is a clearly different angle and entirely fresh footage.
If the choice is between a generic animal topic and a specific species topic of comparable visual quality, always choose the specific species.
examples_preferred: Secretary bird instead of birds of prey
Leaf sheep sea slug instead of sea slug

rules: Editorial premise is a sourced zoological curiosity or accurate animal-behavior explanation, NEVER the chronological description of what appears in the video.

Start from a meaningful verifiable question or unusual fact about food, play, communication, sleep, movement, anatomy, senses, social behavior, adaptations or comparisons. The fact guides the script; real footage illustrates it.
Each story must teach at least one non-obvious independently verifiable fact and explain WHY or HOW; use an accurate comparison or consequence when supported.

Do not narrate incidental clip transitions, camera action, location lists, unconnected scenes or generic filler (e.g. 'agora ele olha', 'aqui ele caminha', 'o vídeo mostra'). A compilation of footage descriptions is NOT editorially acceptable.
Do not invent frequencies, statistics, evolutionary explanations, causal links, diets or behaviors. Record independent scientific/institutional evidence for each central claim; qualify uncertainty.

The first shot and subsequent B-roll need to fit species and claim, but they need not literally show an internal mechanism. If the precise action is not shown, explain it with neutral representative footage or clear labels, without pretending it was filmed.
Keep hook, setup, action, explanation/twist and payoff roles for technical synchronization, but roles organize factual teaching, not a fictional story of one animal through unrelated footage.
Use authentic licensed animal footage as illustrative B-roll, not as a basis to infer undocumented facts or claim that independent clips show the same event/individual.
Never repeat published footage/themes just by changing audio; create genuinely fresh fact angles with new licensed sources and captions.
Maintain Brazilian Portuguese pt-BR throughout, Kokoro pm_alex after real synthesis QA, dynamic concise subtitles and safe optional visual annotations.
Use 3 different cat curiosity angles and 2 other species when verified material exists; avoid quota pressure causing fabrications.

Independent video inspection, attribution, 60–240 s (for revisions from 2026-11-15; legacy 30–45s preserved), <=8 s shot, no >=1s genuine frozen frame, publication_hold and exact @wildvox TikTok-only release remain mandatory.

rules: At least one distinct independent scientific, academic, institutional or expert reference per entry, not a raw animal video URL used as evidence for a biological claim.
Fact, explanation and comparison/consequence must be nonempty distinct statements; review substantive accuracy independently before editorial APPROVE.
Scripts must DEVELOP the fact sheet in natural Brazilian Portuguese, not merely recite what the animal is doing frame by frame.
Shots are supportive real B-roll; do not infer a biological claim only because footage superficially resembles it.
Unverified facts, imprecise comparisons and descriptive-only narration receive VETO even if render/technical tests pass.
No auto-publish of previously rendered or grandfathered clips without independent review under curiosity-first policy.
